title: Splitting stationary sets: Ulam matrices
summary: Every stationary subset of an infinite successor cardinal splits into as many stationary pieces as the size of that cardinal.
abstract: On a regular uncountable cardinal, a closed unbounded set reaches arbitrarily far and contains the limit points it approaches there. A set is stationary when it meets every such set. Although this is a strong largeness condition, it can hold for many disjoint pieces: every stationary subset of the first uncountable ordinal partitions into uncountably many stationary sets. More generally, at any infinite successor cardinal the number of pieces can equal that cardinal’s size, which is the largest possible number of nonempty pieces. None of the pieces can contain a closed unbounded set, since such a set would have to meet every other stationary piece.
